restrictions: Target sha256-r39-prefix-v1: SHA-256 steps 0..38 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; output two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: differential attack using the claw construction for row 16 (solving W16 = K(a0, cv) + f(u) via a van Oorschot-Wiener collision search), a 1 MiB DFS dense-base solver, and the published 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120, Table 21) with the accepted event relaxing row 20 to signed differences.

Cost: time 2^122.98 target compressions (C = 2812). Claw-search kernel 70 operations per 7 lanes, 93 charged per packed evaluation; evaluations per claw 2^11.00, the maximum over 289 chaining values measured at the filed configuration (2^17 slots, 7-byte entries, 2^26-evaluation windows; mean 2^10.970); per-claw success probability 2^-120.71 = side conditions 2^-10.44 (the exact product 2^-9.81 LESS the 0.63-bit adverse deviation measured at a 24-bit prefix, charged), row 17 2^-32, tail rows 18+ 2^-78.273 (99% bootstrap lower bound with Bonferroni 8 on the arithmetic mean of a pooled 140-seed study, stalls at zero, less 0.52 bits for estimator bias). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 122.98 + max(0, 20 - 20) = 122.98, 1.85 bits below our accepted generic entry 744875ec (124.83147) and 1.27 bits below the best AI-valid generic entry awaiting human review, 0c1ef7c3 (124.25213), both priced under the same word-operation convention.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H2, H3, H4, H6, H8, H9 and H11, all score-critical; the time bound additionally under H14, the construction cap (proof.md Sections 7 and 9), which supports no other line. H4 is one premise with three named components, (a) the statistic, (b) uniform expansion, (c) claw selection; component (b), that the free-proposal estimator's frequency equals the attack's frequency over claw-induced expanded words, carries the whole 78.27-bit tail and was declared as a separate H12 in three earlier filings.

Memory 2^20 bytes. Dense solver: 458,752 bytes of linear memory (7 pages, growth refused) + 94,483 module = 553,235. Claw search: 917,504 DP table (2^17 slots at 7 bytes: start point 32 bits, trail length 12, the 8 bits of the distinguished point the index does not fix) + ~60,000 code + ~2,000 condition tables + ~1,200 state + 3,800 advice = ~984,504 peak, 64,072 bytes under 2^20; the code figure is an estimate and is the exposure of the bound. The packed entry is verified not to change the search (9 paired runs identical on every counter). The bound covers the attack's own phases; the memory of the construction work charged under H14 and the campaign envelope (a SAT solver at about 2^26 to 2^28 bytes for our campaign, unknown for the authors' search) is outside it, as proof.md Section 7 states explicitly. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 122.98 + max(0, 20 - 20) = 122.98.

Reconstruction: the complete characteristic and its 140 bit conditions (Appendix A), the filed dense base b1 (B), the dense solver level by level (C), the tail estimator and the limits of its reported bound (D), the claw search, its measured rate curve, its chaining-value schedule and how collision resolution is batched and priced (E), the emitted packed kernel (F), the probability space including the a0-even/u-odd restriction (G), and what each experiment does and does not establish (H) are all in proof.md.

Advice: nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 12 covers the four dense bases (1,024 bytes) and the published characteristic the attack consumes as fixed non-derived data (23 row records and 140 bit conditions, about 1,700-2,800 bytes), total 2,700-3,800. Earlier filings charged 10, counting bases only. preprocessing_log2 = 99 is the cap of premise H14 (2^110 primitive operations / 2812, rounded up), an upper bound on all construction work behind both objects: the audited 496-CPU-hour campaign of restrictions[13] (2^39.21 at 10^9 operations per core-second: shape re-derived, quality bracketed, trail confirmed), the dense solver of Section 4 that produced b1 (a complete search from Table 21 about 2^51.2 target compressions by measured throughput) and the authors' own search for the trail, which is unreported in ePrint 2026/1120, not reproduced here, and bounded by H14 alone. The filed time is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^116.30 (Section 7); Section 10 names that search as the exposure.

Declared heuristics are H2, H3, H4, H6, H8, H9, H11 and H14. There is no H5: it was a tail-transfer premise retired when the tail was measured directly on the filed base. H1 is retired because the ledger does not use it. H10 is disclosed in proof.md Section 9 but constrains no ledger term and is not declared. H12, the uniform-expansion premise of three earlier filings, is folded into H4 as its component (b), text kept in full in Section 9: it is not distinct from H4 and has no evidence distinct from H4's. The numbering is kept so that earlier review findings remain legible.

Provenance of the filed base, corrected: b1 is the first base of the dense solver's logged run (Section 4, Appendix B.1), derived from Table 21 and one tail-interface bit in the module whose memory is charged. It coincides with the published base of Appendix A.4 on rows 4..15 (48 of 72 compared registers bit-for-bit; the 24 that differ are those the SHA-256 relations force when rows 0..3 change) because the solver's search is pinned to the published core and completes it afresh. Filings 1c8ba89c through 2c48b18c said b1 was not a solver output and that its rows 0..3 had been re-solved in the SAT campaign; that was wrong and is withdrawn. The logged run searched one subtree chosen with knowledge of the paper's values, so b1's construction charge (about 2^51.2 target compressions for a complete search) is an estimate anchored to measured throughput. The unrelaxed tail cross-check stays withdrawn as circular. Correctness is unaffected: b1 satisfies every relation and admits rows 16 and 17.

Claw-selected measurement: the per-claw factors are no longer evaluated only on uniform words. experiments/clawdist.py constructs genuine claws through the filed walk function and the base b1 schedule, confirms that every claw has a0 even and u odd, and measures the side-condition rates and the low-bit distribution of W17 on them. The tail remains the factor not measured under that distribution.

Retired heuristics: H1 and H5 are both withdrawn and the numbering is kept so earlier review findings remain legible. H5 was a tail-transfer premise, unnecessary once the tail was measured directly on the filed base. H1 asserted that the fixed target g is at least as good as a random one; no ledger line consumes it, because every per-claw factor is evaluated at g -- the row-17 term is the exact |G17(g)| = 1, the tail study's row-16/17 stages select g and condition on it, and the side conditions are measured on claw-selected variants that target g. There is no random-target quantity anywhere to transfer, so the premise is removed rather than defended.

Two premises that earlier filings asserted are now measured by organizer-run experiments: the splitting estimator's bias (splitting-bias-r39, against a toy with an exactly known answer) and the side-condition factorization under claw selection (the prefix ladder in claw-selected-factors-r39). Two experiments whose checks were identities, clawexp.py and jointside.py, are withdrawn; the algebraic fact jointside.py restated is now a theorem in proof.md rather than an experiment.

Yield of a fixed work budget: the ledger charges an average claw rate. The single-window yield is measured directly -- each vow-rate-stability-r39 trial is one fixed budget, giving 256 samples with mean 8.66 claws, sd 2.96, cv 0.342, first percentile 3 -- so a single window's lower tail is real. It cannot affect the attack: the schedule sums 2^104.21 independent windows, so the relative standard deviation of the total is 0.342 / sqrt(2^104.21) = 2^-53.7, concentrated 48 bits below any precision this ledger reports. Charging the average rate is therefore correct by concentration, not by assumption (proof.md Appendix E.4).

Preprocessing: charged from an audited wall-clock budget. Our own 39-step campaign over the published message shape is logged job by job (52 jobs: 34 UNSAT, 4 SAT, 14 TIMEOUT at a 4-hour cap, 55.5 CPU-hours); all 124 job specifications at the full cap give 496 CPU-hours. What those runs construct and prove: the weight-25 message shape of the published trail is re-derived from the weight bound alone (shape39_hw25, SAT in 484 s); no shape has weight <= 18 (UNSAT); no characteristic of the shape reaches proxy Q <= 70 against the published Q = 80 (UNSAT, 9 s to 3,749 s); the published trail satisfies the window bounds (SAT in 9.2 s); nothing on b1's path ran in the campaign (b1 is the dense solver's output, Section 4). Q in 71..79 within the shape is undecided (three jobs at the cap).

Preprocessing, conversion insensitivity and the cap: converting the campaign's wall-clock at R primitive operations per core-second gives 2^39.21 at R = 10^9, 2^45.85 at 10^11, 2^59.14 at 10^15 and 2^75.75 at 10^20; the filed time_log2 = 122.98 is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^116.30 target compressions (2^127.8 operations), so the conversion rate is not load-bearing. The search by which the authors first found the Q = 80 trail within the shape is unreported in the paper and not reproduced here; it is bounded by premise H14 alone, a cap of 2^110 operations on any computation ever performed (the world's capacity, about 10^22 per second, for a thousand years is 2^108), 17.8 bits below the point where the exponent moves, and preprocessing_log2 = 99 carries that cap. 14 of our own jobs, including the three at Q 71..79, hit the cap undecided.

heuristics.statement: Each chaining value is run for 2^26 trail evaluations in a 2^17-slot distinguished-point table with 7-byte entries and then abandoned for a fresh first block. The ledger charges 2^11.00 evaluations per distinct claw, the maximum over 289 chaining values measured at exactly that configuration (mean 2^10.970, standard deviation 0.007 bits, minimum 2^10.948, maximum 2^10.996), and the premise is that the 2^104.2 chaining values the attack consumes do not, on average, exceed that maximum.
heuristics.scope: The evaluations-per-claw term in the time ledger: 2^11.00 against the measured maximum 2^10.996 and mean 2^10.970. The previous filing charged 2^11.414, the cumulative rate of one 2^30-evaluation run on one chaining value, as a 0.441-bit margin over the single graph it had measured; the margin is replaced by the measured distribution, which is worth 0.414 bits of time.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 289 measured functional graphs (seeds 7, 101..132, 1001..1256; proof.md Appendix E.5 lists every value) to the 2^104.2 the attack uses. The spread between the best and worst of the 289 is 0.05 bits; with three run seeds on each of 32 chaining values at the earlier 128,000-slot configuration, the standard deviation of the per-graph rate once the search's own start-point noise is removed is 0.004 bits (analysis of variance, Appendix E.2b), smaller than the seed-to-seed noise, so the graphs are interchangeable at the ledger's precision. The 2^26 window never reaches the depleted regime the single 2^30 run of Appendix E.2 shows beyond 2^27. The packed 7-byte entry is verified not to change the search: on 9 chaining values the unpacked and packed programs agree on every counter and on the claws found. Per-window overheads are negligible: clearing the flag bytes costs 2^-9.9 operations per evaluation and regenerating the constants less still.
heuristics.limitations: The measurements are reported, not organizer-executed: the research programs clawvow.c and clawvow7.c ran in a container with every command, seed and counter logged in the work tree, and Appendix E.5 carries the per-chaining-value values, but the sandbox cannot run 2^26-evaluation windows. The organizer experiment vow-rate-stability-r39 runs the same search on a 2^20 domain with a substituted even branch and shows only that it executes at a steady rate at that scale. 289 graphs are a sample of 2^104.2; the premise is a statement about their average. The 23 operations of overhead per packed evaluation, including the packing cost of about 0.05 operations per evaluation, are estimated rather than traced (H3).

heuristics.statement: 64 registers, 256-bit words with 7 lanes of 36 bits, 36 bytes per instruction, immediates free. Same convention as 744875ec. The kernel uses 7 peak live registers.
heuristics.scope: The operations-per-evaluation term. C = 2812 word operations per 39-step compression. The claw kernel costs 70 operations per 7-lane word (10.0 per lane evaluation) plus overhead of 23 operations (rounded up from an estimated 22.4, which now includes about 0.05 operations per evaluation for packing the 7-byte table entry).
heuristics.extrapolation: The kernel is counted instruction by instruction by a tracer that is now inside the package: experiments/kernelcount.py rebuilds it on every organizer trial, counts 70 operations for 7 lanes with peak live registers 7, and checks the emitted program against an independent scalar implementation on all 7 lanes of 48 packed vectors per trial with no mismatch. The emitted program is listed line by line in proof.md Appendix F. The overhead (DP test and loop, 6 operations; handler amortized at dp_bits = 7, 16.4 operations) is estimated, not traced.
heuristics.limitations: The convention is self-declared, as in 744875ec. The kernel itself is now traced by an organizer-run experiment, but the 23 operations of DP test, loop and handler overhead are estimated rather than traced and are 25% of the charge; a full trace could move the score by 0.1-0.3 bits. Larger and untested: the 7-way lane packing is worth log2 7 = 2.81 bits against the organizer's scalar price, and that credit rests entirely on the declared convention.

heuristics.statement: The splitting estimator of proof.md Appendix D measures the attack's tail: the probability of the rows-18-to-38 event over the claws the attack generates is at least 2^-78.273. Declared as ONE premise with three named components. (a) The statistic: 2^-78.273 is a 99% bootstrap lower bound, with a Bonferroni factor of 8 for the row-20 selection, on the ARITHMETIC mean of the 140 per-seed q estimates on base b1 with DIFFROW=20, all 20 stalled seeds entered as zero, less 0.52 bits for estimator bias, divided by the exact 2^-64 prefix. (b) Uniform expansion: the frequency of the rows-18-to-38 event over the attack's claw-induced variants, whose expanded words are deterministic functions of (a0, u, cv), equals the frequency the estimator measures by proposing W18..W23 as free, independent, uniform 32-bit words and expanding rows 24..38 from them. (c) Claw selection: fixing W16 and W17 by the claw construction, with whatever bias the vOW search has toward u values with many f-preimages, leaves the tail event's probability unchanged.
heuristics.scope: The tail term, 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits (65% of the exponent); each component moves the exponent one-for-one. Component (a) is the only one with a measured number behind it. Component (b) is the message-freedom model of differential cryptanalysis on SHA-2, and is the model under which the characteristic's published evaluation prices the same uncontrolled part: ePrint 2026/1120, 'Complexity evaluation for collision attack on 39-step SHA-256', counts 168 conditions on (A_i, E_i, W_i) for i >= 16 (its Table 22) and charges 2^168, each condition taken to hold independently with probability 1/2 over free message words; the estimator measures that event on b1 instead of counting conditions, so the two are different statistics resting on one model. Component (b) was declared under a separate ID, H12, in three earlier filings (ec6365d3, 3969c54d, 1c8ba89c); it is declared here as part of H4, with its text kept in full in proof.md Section 9, because it is not a premise distinct from H4 and has no evidence distinct from H4's. The 20 stalled seeds enter at zero, so the bound uses no censoring rule; on the linear scale the stall treatment is worth 0.000384 bits.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 120 seeds were run under a written pre-registration and pooled with the original 20; all 140 values are in proof.md Appendix D.2 and the bound is recomputable: 400,000 resamples at seed 20261017 give 2^-141.734 (percentile) and 2^-141.753 (basic), the more conservative taken; an independent recomputation for this filing from the raw per-seed output files reproduces -141.7532 (basic) and -141.7354 (percentile), with all 20 stalls at row 21. The bias allowance is the weakest step of (a): the 120 completed seeds have sd(log2 q-hat) = 1.257 bits where seven fixed-effort stages at a true population of 2000 would give about sqrt(7/2000)/ln2 = 0.085, implying an effective population near 9.2, the regime the 0.52 bits was measured in, so there is no margin in the allowance; and the calibration toy's stages are state-independent, so it bounds the ratio-estimator component only, not population degeneracy. (b) From a 192-bit free-proposal measure to at most 2^64 variants per chaining value, about 2^30 of them claws, across 2^104.21 chaining values. What is measured under the attack's own distribution: W18 taken from the real expansion on genuine claws is uniform in its low 6 bits (claw-selected-factors-r39, pooled chi-square z about -1.1), one marginal on one of six words. What is measured under the estimator's own measure: the organizer-run row-18 conditional (tail-row18-r39) gives 2^-18.300 against the study's 2^-18.0. The published 2^168 condition count is supporting evidence for the model, not a test of it. (c) From the side conditions and W17, which are measured under claw selection (H8, H9, claw-selected-factors-r39), to the tail, which is not.
heuristics.limitations: Only the first tail stage is organizer-executed: tail-row18-r39 reaches row 18 under free proposals, while rows 19..23 and the run to row 38 remain reported rather than executed, and the per-stage conditionals are not filed, so the bootstrap step is auditable but the per-seed estimates are not. Nothing in the package tests the six-word joint distribution of (b) or the deep tail under the attack's distribution, and no sandbox experiment can: an attack-generated state reaches row 18 with probability about 2^-42 per claw. The W18 check sees 6 bits of 32, on claws from a preimage table that confines u to the 2^21 smallest odd values. All 20 stalls occur at row 21, immediately after the relaxed row 20, which may mean the relaxation defers difficulty; entering them at zero is agnostic about this. A reader who judges the true bias of (a) to exceed 0.52 bits by more than 1.27, or a correlation in (b) or (c) worth more than 1.27 bits, should read this entry as NOT ahead of the best AI-valid generic entry (0c1ef7c3, 124.25213); by more than 1.85 bits, as NOT ahead of the accepted 744875ec.

heuristics.statement: The N = 2^119.70 generated claws behave as sufficiently independent Bernoulli trials for the Poisson success formula, with per-claw probability p = 2^-120.71.
heuristics.scope: The conversion from per-claw probability to total work via Poisson amplification. The Poisson model requires that per-claw successes are approximately independent.
heuristics.extrapolation: Claws from different chaining values come from different walk functions; within a window the 2^15.49 claws share one. Dependence within a window is now measured rather than left open: each trial of claw-selected-factors-r39 derives its own chaining value, no duplicate claw is produced (distinct_claws equals claws in every trial), and the per-trial side-condition successes show no overdispersion against the independent binomial model, the dispersion index being about 1.04 with a standard deviation near 0.09, so clustering above roughly 30% would have shown. The uniformity of W17 under claw selection, which the -32 term rests on, is also binned there.
heuristics.limitations: The measurement is within a window and at this scale: 256 chaining values, about 1,000 claws, and a dispersion test that resolves clustering above roughly 30% and no finer. It does not bound dependence across the 2^104.21 windows the attack consumes, nor heterogeneity between walk functions, and no analysis of the success event's covariance at full scale is supplied. The Poisson conversion is near-linear in N*p at the filed value, so a variance inflation would inflate the required N roughly proportionally.

heuristics.statement: Under the claw-selected, parity-restricted distribution, the full 32-bit joint probability of the two side conditions (rows 8 and 9) is at least the product of the marginals, p8 x p9 = 2^-9.808, less the charged 0.63 bits: at least 2^-10.44. Exact factorization at full width is NOT claimed; the measured prefix deviations are adverse (-0.43 bits at 16 bits, -0.63 at 24) and the larger one is charged in the ledger.
heuristics.scope: The side-condition term of the per-claw exponent, charged at 10.44 bits (Section 7). Each adverse bit at full width beyond the charged 0.63 raises time_log2 one-for-one; a full-width deviation beyond 1.07 bits puts the entry behind 744875ec.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the 16- and 24-bit prefixes resolved under claw selection by claw-selected-factors-r39 (joint prefix rate against the product of the marginal prefix rates: -0.43 and -0.63 bits, each about twice its own resolution of 0.22 and 0.36) to the remaining 8 bits. Under uniform (a0, a1) the factorization is exact, since W8 = C(a1) - a0 makes W8 uniform and independent of a1 for every fixed a1, but that is not the distribution the attack samples. Read as a trend the prefix deviations would reach about 0.8 bits at full width, 0.17 beyond the charge; the charge is the measurement at k = 24, not the trend.
heuristics.limitations: The full-width joint rate is about 2^-10.4, so on the roughly 1,000 claws the sandbox affords its expected count is under 2 and it cannot be measured here. Both measured deviations are adverse and grow with the prefix width, which is the direction that costs the attack; the premise is that the growth does not exceed the charge by more than 0.44 bits at full width. The marginals themselves are measured on genuine claws (p8 2^-3.672, p9 2^-6.158 against the exhaustive -3.830 and -5.978, inside the sample's resolution).

heuristics.statement: Under the claw-selected distribution the fully determined word W17 is uniform over all 32 bits, so |G17(g)| = 1 yields exactly 2^-32 for the row-17 term.
heuristics.scope: The 32-bit row-17 term of the per-claw exponent. |G17(g)| = 1 is exact and verified; this premise is about the denominator, the distribution of W17 over claws.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the low 6 bits: claw-selected-factors-r39 bins W17 over claws and the pooled chi-square is consistent with uniform. The extrapolation is from 6 bits to 32.
heuristics.limitations: The test has little power -- at its band it would miss an eightfold inflation of a single low-bit class about 93% of the time -- and the preimage table confines u to the 2^21 smallest odd values, so any structure in the high bits of W17 is exactly where the test does not look. This is 32 of the 120.71 bits of the per-claw exponent and is a premise, not a measurement, at full width.

heuristics.statement: After conditioning on a genuine claw and on the two side conditions, the row-17 and tail events keep the marginal probabilities the ledger uses, so the three factors may be multiplied into 2^-120.71.
heuristics.scope: The factorization of the per-claw exponent into its three groups. H8 covers the two side conditions against each other and H9 the uniformity of W17; this is the remaining premise, that the groups do not interact.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two conditioning checks on genuine claws, both low-powered and both consistent with independence. W18 from the real expansion on each claw is uniform in its low 6 bits (pooled chi-square z about -1.1), which tests the estimator's uniform-expansion premise at the first tail row under the attack's own distribution. Among claws passing the first side condition, W17's low bit is set 36 times in 85 (z about -1.4). The extrapolation is from these to the full joint event through row 38.
heuristics.limitations: Neither check reaches the tail: conditioning it on side-condition selection needs claws that also pass row 17, costing 2^-32, unreachable at sandbox scale. The W17 check sees one bit on 85 claws and would miss a shift below roughly 20%; the W18 check sees 6 bits of 32. The untested tail carries 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits, so a correlation there moves the exponent one-for-one.

heuristics.statement: The search that produced the published 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120, Table 21), whose effort the paper does not report, cost fewer than 2^110 primitive word operations, i.e. fewer than 2^98.54 target compressions at C = 2812. This is a physical bound on any computation ever performed, not an estimate of that search.
heuristics.scope: The construction-cost component of the time bound, and the filed preprocessing_log2 = 99 (the cap divided by 2812, rounded up). The filed time_log2 = 122.98 is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^116.30 target compressions = 2^127.8 operations, so the premise has 17.8 bits of headroom; preprocessing_log2 = 99 is an upper bound on all construction work behind the two advice objects, the measured campaign (2^39.21 at 10^9 operations per core-second) included. The premise supports no other ledger line, and the success probability does not depend on it.
heuristics.extrapolation: The bound is physical rather than measured: the world's installed computing capacity is of order 10^22 operations per second, and the whole of it for a thousand years performs about 3 x 10^32 = 2^108 operations; the premise allows four times that. For scale, a SAT-based search by an academic group over a fixed message shape (thousands of cores for months) is about 2^63 operations, 47 bits below the premise; the paper's largest reported solver figure is 2^34.2 (Step 1, message finding); our own logged campaign on the same shape is 2^50.7 operations at 10^9 per core-second (proof.md Section 7). The exponent would move only if the authors' search had consumed the planet's capacity for 2^20 thousand years.
heuristics.limitations: No measurement of the authors' search exists and none is supplied; the paper reports no effort figure for it, and it is not reproduced here. No sandbox experiment bears on this premise. It replaces the implicit cap a review extracted from the insensitivity table, and it is deliberately the weakest statement that makes the filed time an upper bound. A reader who requires the historical search to be measured rather than capped will find no measurement in this package; proof.md Section 10 reports the step as this entry's exposure.
